content: Angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitors and angiotensin II receptor blockers (ARBs) are considered the first-line treatment options for individuals who have both diabetes and coronary artery disease. These medications are particularly effective in reducing the risk of progression to more severe kidney disease in patients whose urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio (UACR) is 30 mg/g or higher. Additionally, they play a critical role in preserving renal function by lowering the incidence of cardiovascular events in patients with chronic kidney disease.
